## papers 3.0.0b4

This version rewrites how papers keeps the history of a library for undo.
papers no longer uses git or git-lfs: it keeps its own history, on your
computer, outside the library. Every command that changes a library is a
step of it, and `papers undo` takes back any command together with the
files it moved, renamed, copied or deleted, including a PDF that
`papers add --move` took from `~/Downloads`. There is nothing to set up.
Changes made outside papers (an editor, another program, a synced copy)
are recorded as steps of their own, so that undo never drops them.

It also brings the answers to the issues of Papers Desktop (#117 to #121):
`papers edit --from` and `--set`, `--porcelain`, BibJSON, faster CSL-JSON,
and safe writes of the bibtex.

### The history

- Every command that changes a library records a step in the history of
  the computer (`~/.local/share/papers/history` on Linux). `papers history`
  lists the steps, `papers undo` and `papers redo` move along them (`-n N`
  steps), `papers restore N` goes to step N, also across the branches that
  a change made after an undo starts.
- Undo, redo and restore bring the files back with the bibtex: a moved or
  renamed file goes back where it was, also outside the library; a copy is
  removed; a deleted file comes back from the history. A file is never
  overwritten, and a file whose content changed since (an annotated PDF) is
  left as it is.
- The history keeps up to 500 MB (`history-size`); the oldest steps go
  first, and the files that only they needed go to the trash of the
  system. papers asks before a command that deletes more than the history
  keeps, or so much that recent steps would be dropped (`-y` proceeds).
  `papers config --global keep-deleted-files false` sends deleted files
  straight to the trash of the system.
- A change made outside papers is recorded as a step "changed outside
  papers" at the next command (#120).
- The history follows the library when its folder moves (the library has
  an identifier, `id` in `.papers/config.json`). A copy of a library shares
  the history up to the copy, then branches. `papers export` starts a new
  history.
- All libraries share one store, so that a file is stored once.
  `history-separate` gives a library a store of its own, with its own
  `history-size`. `history-dir` sets where the history is.
- `papers history --all` lists the histories of the computer; `papers
  history --remove [ID]` removes one.
- A library received from someone brings no history, and cannot set where
  the history goes or what it keeps: `history-dir` and
  `keep-deleted-files` are read from the global configuration only.
- When another program writes the bibtex while a command runs, papers does
  not write it (#119), and now also puts back the files that the command
  had moved, copied or deleted.
- `.papers/.gitignore` leaves the folder of papers' internals out of a
  project under git.
- `papers status` in a shallow library says how it stands with its pool:
  `in sync`, `pool changed`, `library changed` or `both changed`, from the
  entries (not the file times), with the command that shows and exchanges
  the changes on its last line. Once in sync, it compares only the
  entries of the pieces of the library, the pool and the origin copies
  that changed since.

### Removed

- The git backup: the `git` and `git-lfs` settings, `papers git`,
  `--git`, `--no-git`, `--git-lfs` and `--restore-files` (ignored, with a
  warning), and the trash of the library with `trash-days` and
  `trash-size`. git and git-lfs are no longer needed.
- The backups of earlier versions (`.papers/backup`,
  `~/.local/share/papers/backups`) are not used and not migrated: undo
  starts with the first command made with this version. `papers history`
  lists them, with their size and the command that deletes them.
- `papers backup` is a deprecated name of `papers history`; `papers
  uninstall` is deprecated (`rm -r .papers`, `papers history --remove`).

### Files

- The `files` setting has a fourth value, `ask`: for each file outside the
  files directory, papers asks whether to move, copy or leave it.
  `papers file rename` and `list --rename` follow the setting, and the
  report lists where each file went.
- `.papers/files.json` holds the checksums of the files (the `checksums`
  setting, true by default); `papers file checksum` writes them, `--check`
  lists the files whose content changed.

### For programs (Papers Desktop)

- `papers edit KEY --from FILE` replaces an entry with one read from a
  file or the standard input (bibtex, RIS, CSL-JSON or BibJSON) (#117).
- `papers edit KEY --set FIELD=VALUE`, `--unset FIELD`, `--key NEWKEY`;
  a change of key is followed by the records of the pools and the
  crossref fields (#122).
- `--porcelain`: the entries a command added, modified, renamed or
  removed, one per line, for programs (#118).
- BibJSON is a format of `list`, `export`, `add` and `edit --from` (#118).
- The CSL-JSON export is about 20 times faster (#118).
- The bibtex is written in one step, and not written when another program
  wrote it since papers read it (#119).
- `--tag` matches whole tags, field names in capitals are read, the parse
  warning is printed once, and a closed pipe ends papers quietly (#121).
